verses.1: Elisha, the prophet, called one of the prophets. He said to him, “Put on your sandals, take this bottle of oil in your hand, and go up the hill.”
verses.2: And you came there, and you saw that there was Yehoshafat’s son, Nimshi’s son. You brought him out from among his brothers, and you put him in a house.
verses.3: And you took the cup of wine, and you poured it over his head. Then you said, “As the Lord has said, ‘You shall be king over Israel.’” You opened the door, and you rushed in. Do not wait any longer.
verses.4: And the young man, the prophet Ramot Gilad, went forth.
verses.5: And he came, and behold, the officers of the army were sitting there. He said to me, “What do you have to say to us, officer?” The officer replied, “To whom among us can I speak?”
verses.6: And he stood up, went into the house, and poured the wine onto his head. Then he said to himself, “As the Lord God of Israel says: ‘You will be king over Israel, as the Lord has declared.’”
verses.7: And you have taken the house of Ahab your priest. I will avenge the blood of my servants, the prophets, and the blood of all Jehovah’s servants, by means of Eizbel.
verses.8: And every house of Abai was destroyed. I knew that Abai would be remembered as a person who was trapped and confined, and who was left behind in Israel.
verses.9: And I gave the house of Ahab as a gift to Joram, son of Nebat, and also the house of Baasha, son of Ahijah.
verses.10: And Eizabel was eaten by the dogs in the part of Judah. There was no grave there. Then the door was opened, and they rushed in.
verses.11: And he went out to his servants and said to them, “Why do you act in this foolish manner? Do you not know the man and his message?”
verses.12: And they said, “False gods! Please give us true gods.” He replied, “In this way and in that way.” He said to them, “As the Lord has said, ‘I will destroy you as kings over Israel.’”
verses.13: And they rushed forward, took someone’s clothes, and put them under the person who was being held up. Then they secured him in the harness. They said, “King Yehu!”
verses.14: And Jehoshaphat, son of Jotham, son of Nimshi, went to Jerusalem. And Jerusalem was under the rule of Jehoshaphat. And all of Israel was under the rule of Ahaziah, king of Aram.
verses.15: And King Jehoshaphat went to Jericho to recover from the wounds he had suffered in the battle against Aram’s king, Hazael. He said, “If there is any hope for us, let no one leave the city to go and report this news to Jericho.”
verses.16: And Jehu rode away, and Jezreel went along with him. When Yoram fell asleep, Jehudah’s king went down to see Yoram.
verses.17: And the prophet stood on the hill in Israel. He saw the prosperity of Jehova coming upon him. He said, “I see His prosperity.” Jehoham said, “Take your chariot and go to them. Tell them, ‘Hush!’”
verses.18: And the rider on the horse went to call him. He said, “Speak thus, O king!” And the king said, “What do you want? Go back to your place.” Then the messenger reported to the king, “The king has arrived there, and he will not return.”
verses.19: And he sent another rider. He came to them and said, “This is what the king Solomon said: ‘What are you going to do?’ So Solomon said to him, ‘Go back to your place.’”
verses.20: And the prophet said, “He will come to them, but he will not return. His behavior will be like that of Jehova son of Nimshi, for in his stupidity, he will act in that manner.”
verses.21: And Johram said, “No!” So he forbade him to ride in his chariot. Then Johram left as king of Israel. He took Yahuhu with him in his chariot. They went out to meet Yahweh. And they found him in a place in the land of Naboth in Judah.
verses.22: And when Yehoham saw Yehuah, he said, “Be quiet, Yehuah!” And he said, “What is this noise? Your mother’s children and her many sons…”
verses.23: And Johram turned his hands around, and he said to Ahaziah, “You are a liar, Ahaziah.”
verses.24: And he filled his hand with seeds. He sowed them among his plants. Then half of them sprouted, and they became plants.
verses.25: And he said to Bidkar, “Throw him into the part of the field belonging to Naboth from Jezreel. This is because I remember that you and he were both riders on donkeys, after Ahab, his father. And Jehovah carried this burden upon him.”
verses.26: If not for the faces of the prophets and their children, I would have seen the light of Jehovah. I will fulfill your request in this part. Now, let them be cast away in that part, as Jehovah commands.
verses.27: And Ahaziah, the king of Judah, saw this. He rushed towards the temple. Yehu followed behind him. Ahaziah ordered that he also be taken to the chariot, which was located on the hill where Jezabel was imprisoned. There, Ahaziah died.
verses.28: And his servants carried him to Jerusalem, and they buried him with his ancestors in the city of David.
verses.29: And in the twelfth year of Jotham’s reign, Ahaziah became king over Judah.
verses.30: And Jehu came, along with Jezreel. He put his eyes on the crown of her head, and he kissed it.
verses.31: And he came to the gate. Then she said, “Hail, my song! Kill his master!”
verses.32: And he turned his face toward the altar, and said, “Who am I? Who are those two or three men who are looking at me?”
verses.33: And Shimthuah said, “Let them be driven away from the walls and from the horses.”
verses.34: And he came, ate, and drank. Then he said, “Please take care of this woman. She is the daughter of a king.”
verses.35: They went to bury her, but they found nothing in her body, except for her bones, her feet, and her hands.
verses.36: And they returned and told him, saying, “This is what the LORD has said: ‘In the land of Israel, dogs will eat the flesh of Izbel.’”
verses.37: And it would be a curse of Isibel, like a thunderbolt upon the faces of the fields in the region of Izrael. They wouldn’t say this about Isibel at all.
